title: Mr. X & The Department of Health (the Department)
text:
Decision
Mr. X & The Department of Health (the Department)
From
Office of the Information Commissioner (OIC)
Case number: OIC-200087-A0A0G1
Published on 9 July 2026
Background
Scope of Review
Preliminary Matters
Analysis and Findings
Decision
Right of Appeal
Whether the Department was justified in refusing the applicant’s request for records relating to its decision not to approve increases to the pensions of medical scientists who retired prior to 1 January 2024 under section 15(1)(a) of the FOI Act, on the grounds that no relevant records were found after all reasonable steps were carried out to locate them
9 July 2026
Background
In a request dated 28 August 2025, the applicant sought records of all records relating to the Department’s decision not to approve the application of pay increases to the pensions of medical scientists who retired prior to 1 January 2024 as per the recommendations contained in the Conal Devine Medical Scientist Assessment Report published in January 2023.
On 17 September 2025, the Department refused the applicant’s request on the basis of section 15(1)(a) of the FOI Act, on the grounds that the records concerned do not exist or cannot be found after all reasonable steps to ascertain their whereabouts have been taken. The Department said that it had conducted electronic searches and engaged in discussions with internal colleagues to search for records relevant to the applicant’s request and had determined that none existed. It further said that no formal decision was either made by it or recommended to it in respect of increases to the pensions of medical scientist retirees as the matter is governed centrally under Department of Public Expenditure Infrastructure, Public Service Reform and Digitalisation (hereafter referred to as the Department of Public Expenditure) policy.
On 6 October 2025, the applicant requested an internal review of the Department’s decision. The applicant said that he had made a similar FOI request to the Department of Public Expenditure (a decision also issued in this case numbered OIC-200088-A0A0G1 by today’s date and is available on our website at
www.oic.ie
) which provided him records of email correspondence between the Health Service Executive (HSE), the Department of Public Expenditure, and the Department of Health during March 2024 on this issue. The applicant said that, given that the Minister has statutory responsibility for approving pay increases to pensioners, it is inconceivable that no departmental records exist around this matter.
On 3 December 2025, the Department issued its internal review decision to affirm its original decision to refuse the request under section 15(1)(a). The Department reiterated that it did not make a decision regarding the application of pay increases to the pensions of medical scientists who retired prior to 1 January 2024. The Department quoted from the recommendation of the Labour Court LCR23079, saying:
“It is apparent from Department of Health Circular 2/2004 that the Minister for Health did not make a decision increasing the pension entitlements of those medical scientist pensioners who had retired before 1 January 2024 in line with the revised salary scales that came into effect for medical scientists in post on 1 January 2024.”
However, the Department said that in the interests of full transparency, it provided the applicant with a record showing its side of the discussion with the Department of Public Expenditure, and the Department of Public Expenditure’s guidance on this matter. The Department of Health also provided the applicant with a letter sent to the Medical Laboratory Scientists Association outlining the Department of Health, Health Service Executive and Department of Public Expenditure’s combined position on this topic.
On 19 January 2026, the applicant applied to this Office for a review of the Department’s decision. On 9 February 2026, the applicant informed this Office that he had made a third similar request for the records to the HSE Pensions Management. The applicant said that the HSE informed him that it does not hold the requested records, but the records would be held by the Department of Health. The applicant said that it is strange that there were fundamental changes made to his pension and yet there are no records held by the Department or the HSE Pensions Management on this matter.
I have now completed my review in accordance with section 22(2) of the FOI Act. In carrying out my review, I have had regard to the submissions made by the Department and the applicant. I have decided to conclude this review by way of a formal, binding decision.
Scope of Review
The scope of this review is solely concerned with whether the Department was justified in its decision to refuse the applicant’s request for records relating to the Department’s decision not to approve the application of pay increases to the pensions of medical scientists who retired prior to 1 January 2024 under section 15(1)(a), on the grounds that no relevant records exist or were found after all reasonable steps were taken to locate them.
Preliminary Matters
It is important to note that the role of this Office is not to determine what records should exist, to adjudicate on how FOI bodies perform their functions generally, nor to act as an alternative dispute resolution mechanism with respect to actions taken by FOI bodies, or by any other parties. Our role is confined to reviewing the decision taken by the FOI body on the applicant’s request for records.
Analysis and Findings
Section 15(1)(a)
Section 15(1)(a) of the Act provides for the refusal of a request where the records sought do not exist or cannot be found after all reasonable steps to ascertain their whereabouts have been taken. The role of this Office in a case such as this is to review the decision of the FOI body and to decide whether that decision was justified. This means that I must have regard to the evidence available to the decision maker and to the reasoning used by the decision maker in arriving at his/her decision and also must assess the adequacy of the searches conducted by the FOI body in looking for relevant records.
The evidence in “search” cases generally consists of the steps actually taken to search for the records along with miscellaneous and other information about the record management practices of the FOI body, insofar as those practices relate to the records in question. It is important to note that the FOI Act is concerned with access to records that a public body holds as opposed to records that a requester considers ought to exist.
Department’s submissions
In its submissions to this Office, the Department said it understood the applicant’s request to comprise a request for records relating to a potential “decision” with respect to the pensions of retired medical scientists.
It said that following receipt of the applicant’s request, inbox searches were conducted by relevant parties for email and letter correspondence relevant to the applicant’s request. It further said that searches were conducted of its EDocs system in respect of any additional documents. However, the Department said that the only related information contained on EDocs were circulars, which are publicly available. The Department said that there was a small number of Departmental officials who would have been involved in either the relevant negotiations and/or circular drafting and publication. It said that all such staff were consulted and all records were searched.
The Department further said that following its decision dated 17 September 2025, a Departmental official spoke with the applicant to explain why his request was refused. It said that this staff member outlined exactly what type of documents did exist and indicated that, while the Department did not consider that such records fell within the scope of the applicant’s request as they was did not relate to a decision that the Department had made, it was nonetheless willing to furnish such documents to the applicant if he so wished. It said that as part of its processing of the applicant’s request for an internal review these documents, while not directly relevant to the request, were provided to the applicant in the interest of transparency.
In conclusion, the Department said that it does not have the sole authority to make such a decision as referred to in the applicant’s request. It said that this responsibility sits with the Department of Public Expenditure and, as such, there were no records relevant to the specific wording of the applicant’s request held by the Department of Health. However, the Department said it is available to engage again with the applicant to refine search terms or provide additional information if sought.
Applicant’s submissions
The Investigating Officer provided the applicant with a summary of the Department’s position as outlined above and provided the applicant with the opportunity to make further submissions of his own.
In response, the applicant said that he is satisfied that the Department is honest in its submissions.
My Analysis
It is important to note that the FOI Act does not require absolute certainty as to the existence or location of records. What the FOI Act requires is that the public body concerned takes all reasonable steps to locate relevant records.
The question I must consider, therefore, is whether the Department has taken all reasonable steps to ascertain the whereabouts of the specific records sought.
The Department’s position is that it holds no records that it comes within the scope of the applicant’s request.
Having carefully considered the Department’s submissions in this matter, I am satisfied that it has provided a sufficiently detailed and cogent explanation as to why no records exist. I accept the Department’s position that it does not have the sole authority to make such a decision as not approving the application of pay increases to the pensions of medical scientists. I also accept that the Department did not actually make a decision in this regard.
In the absence of any evidence to suggest that further searches are warranted in this case, I am satisfied that the Department has carried out all reasonable steps to search for relevant records which are within the scope of the applicant’s request.
Accordingly, I find that the Department was justified in refusing access to records within the scope of the request under section 15(1)(a) of the Act on the basis that the records do not exist or cannot be found after all reasonable steps to ascertain their whereabouts have been taken.
Decision
Having carried out a review under section 22(2) of the FOI Act, I hereby affirm the Department’s decision to refuse the applicant’s request under section 15(1)(a) of the FOI Act on the basis that the records do not exist or cannot be found after it had taken all reasonable steps to ascertain their whereabouts.
Right of Appeal
Section 24 of the FOI Act sets out detailed provisions for an appeal to the High Court by a party to a review, or any other person affected by the decision. In summary, such an appeal, normally on a point of law, must be initiated not later than four weeks after notice of the decision was given to the person bringing the appeal.
